featured_reviews.review_text:
Rajabai Tower, University of Mumbai: The Mumbai University is undoubtedly one of the finest examples of Victorian Neo Gothic
Architecture in Mumbai. It is also an integral part of one of the finest urban ensembles of Victorian buildings in the world. The Rajabai Tower, with its imposing skyline, dominates the skyline of the Fort area, thus further strengthening its classification for reasons of scenic value.
The Mumbai University, designed by Sir Gilbert Scott, is an example of a public project in the city funded by local philanthropists, in this case, the "Cotton King" of Bombay, Premchund Roychund who made a generous contribution of Rupees 4 lakhs towards its construction. As a gesture of acknowledgment, the lofty Rajabai Tower, an awesome structure that rose to a height of 260 feet, was named after his mother. The Library structure adjoining the Rajabai Tower has among the finest ensembles of stained glass in the country while the splendid cross vaulted roof of the Reading Room with its polished timber members, is among the most spectacular architectural interiors in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Rahul
featured_reviews.review_text:
Beautiful place which is seen from city
The 142-year-old Rajabai Clock Tower in South Mumbai’s Fort area, located inside University of Mumbai’s campus, is iconic for its Victorian-Gothic architecture. Built in 1878 by architect Sir George Gilbert Scott, it was commissioned by businessman Premchand Roychand as a tribute to his mother, hence the name. For years, it was the city’s tallest structure, at 285 feet. Rajabai Clock Tower has long been a beacon of the Oval Maidan precinct, a visual delight, and a valuable piece of history for the city. After brilliant restoration work by SNK Consultants, the clock tower was handed over to KSA Lighting Designers in 2017 for lighting the tower, the facade and the interiors of the University Library. Kanchan Puri, principal at the firm, tells us the process of this massive undertaking that was completed recently. After years of darkness, the Rajabai Clock Tower finally glowed up in 2021, literally.

featured_reviews.name: Liviu-Alexandru Buftea (Style)
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you found this place, you had a good guide!

I thought it was Portuguese, but it's actually British. Black as the basaltic rock that rises from the sea, Worli Fort gives a great overview of the bay and the city. It features the classic crenelations and ramparts of the 17th century, and guards the golf from the tip of this tongue of land.

The fort now is not officially maintained or "open to the public". In fact, it seems even locals don’t know about it, but my friend brought me here cause she heard it’s nice. It is accessible for explorer types, and is basically left abandoned.

The fort is simply used by people in this neighborhood for storage, hang out, kids play space, etc. Some clothes left out to dry on the sides, and some barrels and stuff in the rooms below.

Here we met a couple of guys from the city, chilling, listening to cool music, they welcomed us to chat.

It smelled of sea salt, soap, garbage, fish and rats, and the breeze brought “fresh” air from the sea.

As a first time visitor in India, I was in culture shock. Seeing everything was kind of like a dreamy, surreal landscape. So I probably romanticized it too much, for the place is a slum surrounded by a garbage dump, and people here have little chance to better their days, but they were happy, kind and curious.

It was an interesting and humbling experience, worth respect.

featured_reviews.name: Derishta Pillay
featured_reviews.review_text:
At the outset I must say that neither myself nor my husband are huge fans of the usual guided walking tours mainly because we hate being taken to cliched and crowded tourist hotspots, listening to facts straight from the Wikipedia page and jostling for space with other tourists just to return sunburned and underwhelmed. In addition we'd already spent a hectic 5 weeks in India - we were tired, grumpy, waiting to fly back home and not at all looking forward to our last 4 days in Mumbai at all. So basically when our travel companions insisted we book a tour - the scene was set for disaster...
'Bombay Walks' single handedly turned this around and Mumbai actually turned out to be the highlight of our trip! (Nope this is not a sponsored review 😂)

The tour: Arpan's tour extends to the days before and after the actual tour as he offers valuable advice about where to stay/eat/party/shop etc. He speaks perfect English, is pleasant and very easy to communicate with. His passion and love for the city is infectious and you will end his tour enthralled, overwhelmed and completely charmed by Mumbai and it's people - vowing to come back and dig deeper, spend longer and see more. The city tour covers many facets of the city - traveling to hidden gems and local landmarks across the length and breadth of Mumbai. You get to see and experience aspects of Mumbai that you'd never be able to do alone with a guide book or google maps - like traveling on local trains and walking through Worli fishing village and stopping by at small off-the-beaten path temples and churches.

The guide: Arpan is reliable, trustworthy and comes well prepared for the type of group. His talking style is light-hearted and easy going but still knowledgeable and always engaging. He's the type of guide that can tell you interesting facts about the history, architecture and politics of a place but also where to get the best coconut water along the way and which public toilets are ok to use.
We only met Arpan in person on the day of the tour and although we were constantly bombarded with sights, sounds and smells (it is Mumbai after all) - it never once felt like we were just being dragged from point to point whilst he rattled off information but rather that we were spending the day walking around with an old friend.

Target travelers: We're fairly well travelled and yet this is the first time we've ever bothered to leave a tour review - on any platform - I think that in itself indicates how highly we recommend this tour.
This is really a 'must do' in Mumbai.
It's so good we would do this tour again even if it were to cover the exact route we already took. The walking wasn't particular strenuous so it's recommended for any age group it should also be noted that we found that     Arpan was discreetly always conscious of where the group members were and their safety and constantly aware of our surroundings and the locals around us - on that note I would recommend this tour even if you're a single female traveling alone.

When to do it: Try and do this tour on your first full day in Mumbai because it's also a great way to orientate yourself around the city and plan the rest of your time there.

That city that everyone talks about - that's all of India's many faces and layers in one, that accepts everyone, that's everyone's home - regardless of language, religion or creed - Mumbai is THAT city and you'd be crazy if you miss the opportunity to let a born-and-bred local guide you around...

featured_reviews.review_text:
The most striking part of the journey is the uninterrupted view of the Arabian Sea. Driving alongside the coastline with the sea breeze and the horizon in sight provides a sense of openness that is rare in the crowded streets of Mumbai.
​🚇 The Undersea Tunnel
​A major highlight is India’s first undersea tunnel.
​The Transition: Moving from the bright seaside road into the sleek, well-lit 2-km tunnel is a thrill.
​Engineering: The tunnel is wide and surprisingly quiet, passing deep under Girgaon Chowpatty and Malabar Hill.
​⏱️ Efficiency & Speed
​The "Magic" of the Coastal Road lies in the time saved:
​Traffic Bypass: What used to take 45–50 minutes through heavy South Mumbai traffic now takes barely 10 minutes.
​Smooth Surface: The road quality is top-tier, allowing for a very smooth and stable ride.
​📸 Aesthetic Value
​For photography enthusiasts and travelers:
​The interchanges are architecturally impressive, especially when viewed from a distance.
​The road offers a new perspective of the Mumbai Skyline, making it a favorite for "city aesthetic" videos and vlogs.
​💡 Quick Tips for the Visit:
​Speed Limits: Keep an eye on the speed cameras; the limits are strictly enforced for safety.
​No Stopping: While the view is beautiful, stopping to take photos on the main carriageway is not allowed.
​Timing: Try driving during sunset. The golden hour reflections on the sea and the city buildings are breathtaking.
​It is a world-class addition to the city that makes Mumbai feel like a futuristic coastal metropolis!

featured_reviews.name: Ronak Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Mumbai Coastal Road and its underwater tunnel are truly a remarkable achievement in urban infrastructure. The drive beneath the Arabian Sea offers a world-class experience with excellent engineering and smooth traffic flow.
Travel time between Marine Lines, Nariman Point, Haji Ali, and Worli has reduced significantly.
Daily commuting has become far more comfortable, faster, and stress-free for travellers. The tunnel connectivity has greatly eased congestion on major city roads during peak hours. Reaching South Mumbai from the western side of the city is now highly convenient and efficient.
The road quality, lighting, ventilation, and safety arrangements inside the tunnel are exceptionally well maintained. The scenic coastal alignment alongside the Arabian Sea adds a premium driving experience for motorists.
Office commuters, emergency services, and business travellers are receiving major time-saving benefits.
The zero-toll facility is an excellent public benefit and makes the project even more appreciable.
Connectivity between Marine Drive, Breach Candy, Haji Ali, and Worli has become smooth and seamless. This project is undoubtedly one of Mumbai’s finest modern infrastructure developments and a proud achievement for the city.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellant place for Morning Walker, kids and families.

HERITAGE GARDEN: De-stressing and Rejuvenating in a Different World

Pramod Chavan

Surrounded by high-rise concrete buildings and glass-fronted skyscrapers opposite the Glen Towers on Cliff Avenue Road in Powai, a Heritage Garden means Bharat Ratna Atal Bihari Vajpayee Udyan is a de-stressing and rejuvenating world.

The special thing about this ten-acre park is that it is not just a park for one class or one age group. On one side are college students on the fence and on the other a group of senior citizens reminiscing. Here, among the youth the guitar tunes, and among the senior citizens, someone easily makes the flute tunes, mesmerizing the entire atmosphere.

Apart from the magnificence of the surrounding residential complexes, it is the right space for yoga enthusiasts with its many offices and commercial setups. It has become a place for those who practice regular and mixed martial arts.

The landscaped lawns, a separate play area for children, a Japanese-style Miyawaki patch on one side and a circular walking path that winds around the periphery of the park make the Heritage Garden a pleasant place to spend an evening with your loved ones.

Heritage Garden is one of the main places for morning walkers in Powai and the surrounding area. There is a beautiful gazebo apart from benches at regular intervals. It also has a beautiful artificial pond which often has beautiful lotus flowers.

The stone structure along the circular walkway attracts the attention of all new visitors. There is also a restroom on one side of the park.

Another special feature of this park is that some other parks in the city often organize events, so people coming to the park have a lot of trouble. However, events or other mass activities are still not allowed here without permission.

The man-made wells located at the corners of the park are used the most during monsoons. But it has not been able to escape from the habit of people coming to the garden to throw large amounts of waste.

Garden gates open at 5 am, after that they are closed from 12 noon to 4.30 pm... and open again from 4.30 pm to 10 pm.
